fields.meta_title: Returns Automation From Request to Restock | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build returns automation that applies your return policy, offers an exchange first, grades items at the dock, and counts return reasons.
fields.h1: Build Returns Automation That Applies Your Policy to Every Return
fields.hero_description: Build returns automation that sorts each request by your return policy and keeps every return in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds for Each Return
fields.features_subheading: Each part runs one stage of a return, and all of them write to the same return record.
fields.feature_1:
Your return policy, applied to every request

Write the return window, the final-sale items, and any exceptions in plain English. The app tests each request against those rules before a label goes out and saves the result.
fields.feature_2:
Exchange or credit offered before a refund

The return portal offers a different size or store credit before it offers money back. You choose the products that qualify and the bonus added to credit, and each pick is recorded.
fields.feature_3:
Return labels from your carrier account

Connect your store platform and your shipping carrier through their APIs. The app creates the return label, follows the tracking scans, and marks the order when the box heads back.
fields.feature_4:
A grade and a photo for every returned item

Staff at the dock pick a grade for each item on a phone or tablet and add a photo when it is damaged. The grade sets the item's next stop: a stock bin, an outlet shelf, or a person.
fields.feature_5:
Return reasons counted by product

Customers pick a reason with each return, and the dashboard counts reasons by product as they arrive. If a product passes a threshold you set, its merchandiser gets a Slack alert.
fields.feature_6:
The returns app's code, in your GitHub

Export the full code of the returns app to your GitHub repository on paid plans. Engineers can read how each refund decision is recorded and extend the app like any other codebase.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Stops on a Return's Way Back
fields.tab_content_1:
Within 30 days of delivery, the label goes out

Cobblefen Outdoor takes returns within 30 days of delivery. This week brought 64 requests, and the app checked each delivery date and final-sale flag. A return label went by email to the 58 that passed. The other 6 went to Ysolde Harrowby on support: 4 past 30 days and 2 final-sale items.
fields.tab_content_2:
Size 9.5 ships on the carrier's first scan

Imelda Quarrington starts a return of trail boots in size 9 from Larkmoor Footwear order #31876. The portal offers size 9.5 or store credit of $158 first, then a $148 refund. The credit is the $148 price plus a $10 bonus. She picks size 9.5, and the exchange order ships when the carrier first scans her return.
fields.tab_content_3:
The lamp with a cracked base goes to review

At Brindlewood Home's receiving dock, items graded A go back to stock. Items graded C need a photo and go to Nerys Ramsden, the returns lead, for review. Casimir Vantongeren grades return #4471, which holds 3 items: a throw and a vase pass as grade A. The table lamp has a cracked base and is graded C.
fields.tab_content_4:
26 of 40 jacket returns say it runs small

Ferncastle Apparel's Monday report counts return reasons by product. Last month the Harbor rain jacket came back 40 times: 26 said it runs small, 9 changed their minds, and 5 arrived damaged. When one reason covers more than half of a product's returns, Philippa Okwuosa, the merchandiser, gets a direct message.

fields.howto_description: Seven steps to turn your return policy into returns automation with clear rules and grades, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Write your return policy as rules
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Choose what shows before a refund
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Connect the systems around a return
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write your return policy down as rules a machine can test: the window in days from delivery, which items are final sale, and the condition an item must arrive in. Mark each rule as automatic or as one that sends the request to a person.
fields.howto_step_2_des: For every outcome, name the action and the owner. An approved request gets a label by email, a declined one gets the reason in writing, and an exception lands in the support queue. Keep the list short enough to learn in one read.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Decide what the portal shows before money back. Offer exchanges only on sizes in stock, and try a small credit bonus, such as $10, on one product line for a month before you extend it to the rest of the catalog.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Connect the store platform that holds your orders, the carrier that prints return labels, and the payment system that issues refunds, each through its API. Describe the flow in a prompt, and Emergent builds the portal and the rules on top.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Define grades for the receiving dock
fields.howto_step_5_des: Agree on 2 or 3 grades that receiving staff can apply without a manual, and give each grade one next stop. Require a photo for any grade that holds up a refund, and name the person who reviews those photos.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Pull 20 returns from last month, including a late request, a final-sale item, and a damaged one. Run them through the app and check that each gets the outcome it got by hand. Fix any rule by prompting, then run the set again.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Go live on one product line
fields.howto_step_7_des: Turn on the portal for one product line first, such as footwear, and watch the support queue for a week. Read the first monthly reasons report before you add the next line, and move the rest over once the queue stays small.

faq_plan.a: Returns automation is software that runs each product return by rules you set. It checks the request against your policy, sends the return label, offers an exchange or credit, records the grade when the item arrives, and logs the refund. People see only the requests the rules send them.

faq_plan.q: How do I set up returns automation?
faq_plan.a: Start from your written return policy and turn each line into a rule: the return window and who reviews the exceptions. Then decide what the portal offers before a refund and how the dock grades items. In Emergent's AI automation builder, you describe those rules in plain English and get a working returns app with its database.

faq_plan.q: How do online stores choose returns automation software?
faq_plan.ref: how online stores choose returns automation software
faq_plan.a: Run your own return policy through each option instead of watching a demo. Check that it reads orders from your store platform, prints labels with your carrier, handles exchanges as well as refunds, and lets you query the return data. Price it at your busiest month's volume. Emergent builds the returns app from a prompt, and each return lands in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: How do returns automation platforms upsell customers during a return?
faq_plan.ref: how returns automation platforms upsell customers during returns
faq_plan.a: They upsell by showing an exchange or store credit before the refund. A customer returning boots in the wrong size sees the right size first, and store credit can carry a small bonus over the refund amount. You can also show a matching product next to the credit offer. Keep the sizes customers swap into in stock by reordering them through procurement automation.

faq_plan.q: How does returns automation software check for fraudulent returns?
faq_plan.ref: how returns automation software prevents fraudulent returns
faq_plan.a: It compares each return with its order and flags the ones that do not match, for a person to decide. Useful checks: an item that was never on the order, a request outside the window, or a received SKU that differs from the one shipped. Also flag any customer whose returns in 90 days pass a number you choose. A flag holds the refund; it does not accuse anyone.

faq_plan.q: How does returns automation help a store grow without adding staff?
faq_plan.ref: how returns automation can help your business grow
faq_plan.a: It lets order volume rise without the returns workload rising at the same pace. Rules approve every request inside the policy and send the label without anyone typing. People handle only the exceptions, and the hours support spent on routine returns can go to questions from customers who have not bought yet.

faq_plan.q: How does returns automation lead to long-term growth?
faq_plan.ref: how returns automation can lead to long-term growth
faq_plan.a: It leads there through the data it collects. Every return carries a product and a reason, and a monthly count shows which size charts, photos, or suppliers sit behind the most returns. Fix one, and next month's count shows whether the fix worked. Returns are one part of ecommerce automation, and the same order record can feed both.

faq_plan.q: How do returns automation systems handle image uploads for item verification?
faq_plan.ref: how returns automation systems handle image uploads for item verification
faq_plan.a: They attach each photo to the return and the item it shows. A customer can upload one with the request, and receiving staff add their own when they grade the item. A person compares the two before approving a damage claim. In an app built with Emergent, every photo stays with its return record in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: How do you calculate the total cost savings from returns automation?
faq_plan.ref: how to calculate total cost savings from returns automation
faq_plan.a: Add three monthly figures and subtract one. First, minutes saved per return times returns handled, times the hourly cost of the person who handled them. Second, refunds that became exchanges or store credit. Third, the value of items restocked sooner after grading. Subtract what the software costs to run, and compare the result with the month before you switched.

faq_plan.q: How does returns automation improve warehouse efficiency?
faq_plan.ref: how returns automation improves warehouse efficiency
faq_plan.a: It tells receiving what is in each box before anyone opens it, because the return label links to a record of the items and the reason. Restockable items go straight to a bin instead of a holding pile. Items graded defective can go back to the supplier for a credit, which accounts payable automation then matches against the next bill.
